questions.text: After the 1971 war, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto took over as President and Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan in which month?
questions.explanation: Bhutto assumed the offices of President and Chief Martial Law Administrator on 20 December 1971, after Yahya Khan resigned in the wake of the loss of East Pakistan.

questions.text: On behalf of Pakistan, the Instrument of Surrender at Dhaka on 16 December 1971 was signed by which officer?
questions.explanation: Lt. Gen. A.A.K. Niazi, commander of Pakistani forces in the East, signed the Instrument of Surrender before Indian Lt. Gen. Jagjit Singh Aurora.

questions.text: Following the 1971 war, approximately how many Pakistani military and civilian personnel were held as prisoners of war by India?
questions.explanation: India held around 93,000 Pakistani prisoners of war and civilian internees, who were repatriated over the following two years under the Simla Agreement framework.

questions.text: The Hamoodur Rahman Commission was set up by the Government of Pakistan to inquire into which event?
options: The circumstances of the 1971 war and the fall of Dhaka
questions.explanation: Headed by Chief Justice Hamoodur Rahman, the commission investigated the causes of the military defeat in East Pakistan in 1971.

questions.text: Under the Simla Agreement of 1972, the ceasefire line in Kashmir was renamed as the
questions.explanation: The 1972 Simla Agreement between Pakistan and India renamed the earlier ceasefire line in Kashmir as the Line of Control.

questions.text: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's land reforms of 1972 fixed the ceiling on individual landholding at how many acres of irrigated land?
questions.explanation: The 1972 land reforms reduced the permissible ceiling to 150 acres of irrigated land and 300 acres of unirrigated land.

questions.text: The Pakistan National Alliance, an opposition coalition formed after the disputed general election of 1977, was formed to oppose the government of which party?
questions.explanation: The Pakistan National Alliance was a multi-party coalition formed to protest the Pakistan Peoples Party's victory in the March 1977 elections.

questions.text: In which year was former Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto executed?
questions.explanation: Bhutto was hanged on 4 April 1979 at Rawalpindi after being convicted of conspiracy to murder.

questions.text: General Zia-ul-Haq formally assumed the office of President of Pakistan in
questions.explanation: Zia-ul-Haq became President on 16 September 1978, succeeding Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry.

questions.text: The Hudood Ordinances, introducing Islamic criminal punishments into Pakistani law, were promulgated in
questions.explanation: The Hudood Ordinances were promulgated by General Zia-ul-Haq's government in February 1979.

questions.text: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, providing for compulsory deduction of zakat, was introduced in
questions.explanation: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance was promulgated in 1980 as part of General Zia-ul-Haq's Islamization measures.

questions.text: The Movement for the Restoration of Democracy (MRD), an alliance of opposition parties against military rule, was launched in
questions.explanation: The MRD was formed in 1981 to campaign for an end to General Zia-ul-Haq's martial law and the restoration of democratic government.

questions.text: The long-running military standoff between Pakistan and India over the Siachen Glacier began in
questions.explanation: Fighting over Siachen began in April 1984 after Indian forces occupied the glacier, making it one of the world's highest battlegrounds.

questions.text: General Zia-ul-Haq held a national referendum seeking a mandate for his Islamization programme and continuation in office in
questions.explanation: The referendum was held in December 1984, with the government claiming overwhelming public endorsement.

questions.text: Pakistan's first general election held on a non-party basis under General Zia-ul-Haq took place in
questions.explanation: The February 1985 elections were held without party affiliation on the ballot, after which Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister.

questions.text: Prime Minister Muhammad Khan Junejo's government was dismissed by President Zia-ul-Haq in
questions.explanation: Zia-ul-Haq dismissed the Junejo government on 29 May 1988, shortly before his own death in an air crash.

questions.text: The 1988 Ojhri Camp disaster, in which an ammunition depot exploded causing heavy casualties, took place in which city?
questions.explanation: The explosion at the Ojhri Camp ammunition store occurred in Rawalpindi in April 1988, killing more than a hundred people.

questions.text: Benazir Bhutto's first government was dismissed by President Ghulam Ishaq Khan in
questions.explanation: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan dismissed Benazir Bhutto's first government in August 1990 on charges of corruption and misgovernance.

questions.text: Nawaz Sharif was sworn in as Prime Minister of Pakistan for the first time in
questions.explanation: Nawaz Sharif first became Prime Minister in November 1990, after his alliance won the elections that followed Benazir Bhutto's dismissal.

questions.text: In July 1993, President Ghulam Ishaq Khan and Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif both resigned under an arrangement brokered by the Chief of Army Staff, General
questions.explanation: General Abdul Waheed Kakar mediated the political deadlock, leading both the President and the Prime Minister to resign and a caretaker government to be installed.

questions.text: Benazir Bhutto's second government was dismissed by President Farooq Leghari in
questions.explanation: President Farooq Leghari dismissed Benazir Bhutto's second government in November 1996 amid allegations of corruption.

questions.text: The military takeover led by General Pervez Musharraf that removed the government of Nawaz Sharif took place on
questions.explanation: General Pervez Musharraf assumed power on 12 October 1999 after his removal as Army Chief was blocked and the government was overthrown.

questions.text: The Kargil conflict between Pakistani and Indian forces in the mountains of Indian-administered Kashmir took place in
questions.explanation: Fighting in the Kargil sector occurred between May and July 1999, ending after international pressure led to a Pakistani withdrawal.

questions.text: General Pervez Musharraf held a referendum seeking public endorsement to continue as President for a further five years in
questions.explanation: The referendum was held in April 2002 and was used to extend Musharraf's presidency.

questions.text: The 2007 Lawyers' Movement in Pakistan primarily demanded the restoration of which suspended Chief Justice?
questions.explanation: The lawyers' agitation of 2007-09 sought the reinstatement of Chief Justice Iftikhar Muhammad Chaudhry, who was eventually restored in March 2009.

questions.text: The security operation against militants holed up in Islamabad's Lal Masjid (Red Mosque) took place in
questions.explanation: The operation, launched in July 2007, ended a prolonged standoff between security forces and armed militants at the mosque complex.

questions.text: Former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated in December 2007 while campaigning in
questions.explanation: Benazir Bhutto was assassinated after an election rally in Rawalpindi on 27 December 2007.

questions.text: The general election of February 2008, which ended General Musharraf's period as an army-backed President, was won by which party?
questions.explanation: The Pakistan Peoples Party won the largest number of seats in the 2008 election and led the coalition government that followed.

questions.text: The devastating earthquake that struck northern Pakistan on 8 October 2005 was centred near
questions.explanation: The epicentre lay near Muzaffarabad in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and the quake killed over 70,000 people across the region.

questions.text: The catastrophic floods of 2010, among the worst in Pakistan's history, were caused by exceptionally heavy monsoon rains along which river system?
questions.explanation: Heavy monsoon rains swelled the Indus and its tributaries, submerging large areas from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa down to Sindh.

questions.text: Al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden was killed by a US special forces raid in May 2011 in which Pakistani city?
questions.explanation: The raid took place in Abbottabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on 2 May 2011.

questions.text: The attack on the Army Public School in Peshawar, one of the deadliest terrorist attacks in Pakistan's history, occurred in
questions.explanation: Militants attacked the school on 16 December 2014, killing over a hundred students and staff.

questions.text: Operation Zarb-e-Azb, a major military offensive against militant strongholds, was launched in June 2014 in
questions.explanation: The operation targeted militant sanctuaries in North Waziristan following an attack on Karachi airport.

questions.text: Pakistan's nuclear weapons tests of May 1998 were officially given which code name?
questions.explanation: The six underground tests conducted on 28 May 1998 were officially designated Chagai-I.

questions.text: Pakistan's first indigenously developed satellite, Badr-1, was launched in
questions.explanation: Badr-1 was launched on 16 July 1990 aboard a Chinese Long March rocket, making Pakistan one of the first developing countries to build and operate its own satellite.

questions.text: The Economic Cooperation Organization, formed in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, succeeded an earlier grouping known as
questions.explanation: ECO succeeded the Regional Cooperation for Development, which the three countries had formed in 1964.

questions.text: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), of which Pakistan is a founding member, was established in
questions.explanation: SAARC was founded in 1985 at a summit in Dhaka, bringing together seven South Asian states including Pakistan.

questions.text: Following the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, Pakistan began hosting very large numbers of Afghan refugees from
questions.explanation: After the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan in December 1979, millions of Afghan refugees crossed into Pakistan over the following decade.

questions.text: Pakistan formally joined the US-led international coalition against terrorism following the attacks of
questions.explanation: Pakistan became a key ally in the campaign against terrorism after the September 11, 2001 attacks in the United States.

questions.text: Which language is the mother tongue of the majority of the population in Punjab province?
questions.explanation: Punjabi is the predominant first language spoken in Punjab, Pakistan's most populous province.

questions.text: Which language is predominantly spoken in Sindh province?
questions.explanation: Sindhi is the principal language of Sindh and one of the oldest written languages of the subcontinent.

questions.text: Pashto is the predominant language of which province of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Pashto is spoken by the majority of the population in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and by Pashtun communities in northern Balochistan.

questions.text: Balochi and Brahui are the two major languages spoken in
questions.explanation: Balochi and Brahui, two linguistically unrelated languages, are both widely spoken across Balochistan.

questions.text: Shina, Balti and Burushaski are among the languages spoken in
questions.explanation: Gilgit-Baltistan is linguistically diverse, with Shina, Balti, Burushaski and Wakhi all spoken across its valleys.

questions.text: Basant, a traditional kite-flying festival historically associated with Lahore, marks the arrival of which season?
questions.explanation: Basant traditionally celebrated the coming of spring and was especially popular in Punjab.

questions.text: Sindhi Cultural Day is traditionally marked by people wearing the Ajrak along with which item of headwear?
questions.explanation: On Sindhi Cultural Day, people across Sindh wear the traditional Sindhi cap together with the block-printed Ajrak shawl.

questions.text: The Shandur Polo Festival, held at the world's highest polo ground, is traditionally contested between teams from Chitral and
questions.explanation: The annual festival at Shandur Pass features a polo match between teams representing Chitral and Gilgit.

questions.text: The Kalash people of Chitral celebrate their winter festival, marking the new year, which is known as
questions.explanation: Chaumos (also spelt Choimus) is the Kalash midwinter festival, celebrated with dancing, music and ritual bonfires.

questions.text: Sajji, a dish of whole lamb or chicken marinated and roasted over charcoal, is a specialty of which province's cuisine?
questions.explanation: Sajji is a signature dish of Balochi cuisine, traditionally cooked using minimal spices to preserve the meat's natural flavour.

questions.text: Chapli kabab, a spiced minced-meat patty fried flat, is a culinary specialty most associated with which city?
questions.explanation: Chapli kabab originates from Peshawar and the surrounding Pashtun belt of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

questions.text: Sarson ka saag served with makai ki roti is a traditional winter dish particularly associated with
questions.explanation: This mustard-greens dish with cornbread is a classic winter staple of rural Punjab.

questions.text: Attan, an energetic circular dance performed at weddings and festive occasions, is traditionally associated with which people of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Attan is a traditional Pashtun dance performed at celebrations across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and among Pashtun communities in Balochistan and Afghanistan.

questions.text: Bhangra, a lively dance traditionally performed at harvest time, originated in which province of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Bhangra developed as a harvest celebration dance among the farming communities of Punjab.

questions.text: The Pakol, a soft, rolled woollen cap, is traditionally worn by men in which region of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Pakol is a traditional cap of the mountainous north, worn in Chitral, Gilgit-Baltistan and neighbouring parts of Afghanistan.

questions.text: The traditional dress of Baloch women is particularly noted for its elaborate
questions.explanation: Baloch women's dresses are famous for heavy embroidery combined with small mirror pieces sewn into the fabric.

questions.text: The Peshawari chappal, a traditional handmade leather sandal, takes its name from which city?
questions.explanation: The Peshawari chappal is a rustic leather sandal that originated in Peshawar and the surrounding region.

questions.text: The rubab, a plucked lute-like instrument central to Pashtun folk and classical music, is most closely associated with which province?
questions.explanation: The rubab is the signature instrument of Pashtun music and is closely identified with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

questions.text: The alghoza, a wind instrument made of a pair of joined flutes played simultaneously, is a traditional folk instrument of Sindh and
questions.explanation: The alghoza is a double-flute instrument widely used in the folk music of both Sindh and Balochistan.

questions.text: The chimta, a metal percussion instrument shaped like a pair of tongs, is a familiar accompaniment in the folk music of
questions.explanation: The chimta is commonly used to keep rhythm in Punjabi folk music and bhangra performances.

questions.text: Ho Jamalo, a lively Sindhi folk dance traditionally performed on occasions of joy and celebration, originates from which province?
questions.explanation: Ho Jamalo is a well-known folk dance of Sindh performed at festive and celebratory gatherings.

questions.text: Lahore, the provincial capital of Punjab, is popularly known by which nickname on account of its many parks and gardens?
questions.explanation: Lahore's numerous Mughal-era and colonial gardens have earned it the popular title 'City of Gardens'.

questions.text: Karachi, Pakistan's largest city, is popularly nicknamed the
questions.explanation: Karachi is popularly called the 'City of Lights' on account of its vibrant nightlife and status as Pakistan's commercial hub.

questions.text: Multan, one of the oldest cities of the subcontinent and home to numerous Sufi shrines, is popularly known as the
questions.explanation: Multan's many Sufi shrines and mausoleums have earned it the popular title 'City of Saints'.

questions.text: Quetta, the capital of Balochistan, is popularly associated with its orchards and known informally as Pakistan's
questions.explanation: Quetta and its surrounding valleys are known for extensive fruit orchards, particularly apples and grapes, earning it the nickname 'Fruit Garden of Pakistan'.

questions.text: The Urdu poet Faiz Ahmed Faiz was awarded the Soviet Union's Lenin Peace Prize in
questions.explanation: Faiz Ahmed Faiz received the Lenin Peace Prize in 1962 in recognition of his progressive poetry.

questions.text: Allama Iqbal, Pakistan's national poet, is popularly honoured with the title
questions.explanation: Iqbal is widely known as Shair-e-Mashriq, the 'Poet of the East', for his philosophical poetry in Urdu and Persian.

questions.text: Fatima Jinnah, sister of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, is popularly remembered by the honorific title
questions.explanation: Fatima Jinnah is known as Madar-e-Millat, meaning 'Mother of the Nation'.

questions.text: Josh Malihabadi, a leading twentieth-century Urdu poet, is popularly known by the title
questions.explanation: Josh Malihabadi earned the title Shair-e-Inqilab for the revolutionary and passionate character of his verse.

questions.text: The novel Raja Gidh, a landmark of modern Urdu fiction, was written by
questions.explanation: Raja Gidh, published in 1981, is one of the best-known novels of Pakistani writer Bano Qudsia.

questions.text: The short story Toba Tek Singh, depicting the trauma of Partition, was written by
questions.explanation: Toba Tek Singh, one of Saadat Hasan Manto's most famous short stories, satirises the absurdity of Partition through an asylum inmate.

questions.text: The Urdu poet Habib Jalib is best remembered for his poetry of protest against military rule, particularly the poem
questions.explanation: Habib Jalib's poem 'Dastoor' became an anthem of resistance against Ayub Khan's 1962 constitution and later against martial law.

questions.text: The Urdu poetess Parveen Shakir, known for blending classical ghazal form with modern feminine sensibility, is best remembered for her collection
questions.explanation: Khushbu, published in 1976, established Parveen Shakir as one of the leading modern Urdu poets.

questions.text: Bulleh Shah, one of the most celebrated Sufi poets of the subcontinent, composed chiefly in which language?
questions.explanation: Bulleh Shah's mystical verse, still widely sung today, was composed mainly in Punjabi.

questions.text: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai, revered Sufi poet and author of the Shah Jo Risalo, is buried at his shrine in
questions.explanation: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai's shrine is located at Bhit Shah in Sindh, where his poetry remains central to Sindhi culture.

questions.text: Sachal Sarmast, a celebrated Sufi poet of Sindh, is popularly known by the title
questions.explanation: Sachal Sarmast composed verse in several languages, earning him the title 'Poet of Seven Languages'.

questions.text: Khushal Khan Khattak, regarded as the father of Pashto literature, was, besides being a poet, also known as a
questions.explanation: Khushal Khan Khattak was a seventeenth-century Pashtun tribal chief who took up arms against Mughal rule while composing a large body of Pashto poetry.

questions.text: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, who brought international fame to Pakistani music, was a celebrated master of which genre?
questions.explanation: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan was internationally renowned as a master of Qawwali, Sufi devotional singing.

questions.text: Ghazal singer Mehdi Hassan is popularly remembered by the honorific title
questions.explanation: Mehdi Hassan's mastery of the ghazal earned him the widely used title 'King of Ghazal'.

questions.text: Singer and actress Noor Jehan is popularly remembered in Pakistan by the title
questions.explanation: Noor Jehan is affectionately known as Malika-e-Tarannum, 'Queen of Melody', for her decades-long singing career.

questions.text: Sadequain, one of Pakistan's most celebrated modern artists, is particularly known for combining painting with which traditional art form?
questions.explanation: Sadequain fused bold calligraphic script, especially of Quranic verses, with his expressive painting style.

questions.text: The Chughtai Museum, dedicated to the pioneering modernist painter Abdur Rahman Chughtai, is located in
questions.explanation: The museum, housed at the artist's former residence, is located in Lahore.

questions.text: Painter and sculptor Ismail Gulgee, known for his abstract and calligraphic art, was also skilled as a
questions.explanation: Besides painting, Gulgee produced large-scale sculptures and is remembered as one of Pakistan's foremost modern artists.

questions.text: The Edhi Foundation, Pakistan's largest welfare and ambulance service organization, was founded by
questions.explanation: Abdul Sattar Edhi built the Edhi Foundation into the country's largest privately run social welfare network.

questions.text: The Faisal Mosque in Islamabad, funded by Saudi Arabia and completed in 1986, was designed by architect
options: Louis Kahn of the United States
questions.explanation: The Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay won the international competition to design the Faisal Mosque, giving it its distinctive tent-like shape.

questions.text: Pakistan won the Cricket World Cup in 1992 under the captaincy of
questions.explanation: Pakistan won its first Cricket World Cup title in 1992 under Imran Khan, defeating England in the final.

questions.text: Pakistan's hockey team most recently won an Olympic gold medal in
questions.explanation: Pakistan has won three Olympic hockey gold medals (1960, 1968 and 1984), with 1984 being the most recent.

questions.text: Pakistan won its first Hockey World Cup title in
questions.explanation: Pakistan won the inaugural Hockey World Cup, held in Barcelona in 1971.

questions.text: Squash legend Jahangir Khan remained unbeaten in competitive matches for a record period of nearly
questions.explanation: Jahangir Khan went unbeaten from 1981 to 1986, one of the longest winning streaks in professional sport.

questions.text: Hashim Khan, regarded as the founder of Pakistan's squash dynasty, won his first British Open title in
questions.explanation: Hashim Khan won the British Open Squash Championship for the first time in 1951, beginning Pakistan's long dominance of the sport.

questions.text: Jansher Khan emerged as the dominant force in world squash in the late 1980s, succeeding fellow Pakistani player
questions.explanation: Jansher Khan took over as the leading squash player of his era after Jahangir Khan's long period of dominance.

questions.text: Mohenjo-daro, a UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site of the Indus Valley Civilization, is located in which province?
questions.explanation: Mohenjo-daro, one of the world's earliest major urban settlements, lies on the right bank of the Indus in Sindh.

questions.text: Taxila, an ancient centre of learning and UNESCO World Heritage Site with significant Buddhist archaeological remains, is located near
questions.explanation: Taxila lies near Rawalpindi in Punjab and was once a renowned centre of Gandhara Buddhist civilization and learning.

questions.text: Lahore is the provincial capital of
questions.explanation: Lahore, the second-largest city of Pakistan, serves as the capital of Punjab province.

questions.text: Karachi serves as the provincial capital of
questions.explanation: Karachi, Pakistan's largest city and chief seaport, is the provincial capital of Sindh.

questions.text: Peshawar is the provincial capital of
questions.explanation: Peshawar, one of the oldest cities of South Asia, is the provincial capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

questions.text: Quetta is the provincial capital of
questions.explanation: Quetta serves as the capital of Balochistan, Pakistan's largest province by area.

questions.text: The capital of Gilgit-Baltistan is
questions.explanation: Gilgit serves as the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan.

questions.text: Which city serves as the federal capital of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Islamabad has served as the federal capital of Pakistan since the seat of government was shifted there in the 1960s.

questions.text: How many provinces make up the federation of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Pakistan is made up of four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

questions.text: Among Pakistan's four provinces, which has the smallest total area?
questions.explanation: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is the smallest of the four provinces in land area, while Balochistan is the largest.

questions.text: Gilgit-Baltistan is administered separately from Pakistan's four provinces mainly because of its association with the unresolved
questions.explanation: Gilgit-Baltistan's final constitutional status remains linked to the wider Jammu and Kashmir dispute, so it is not formally one of Pakistan's provinces.

questions.text: Azad Jammu and Kashmir has its own president, prime minister and legislative assembly, and consequently is not represented in Pakistan's
questions.explanation: As a self-governing territory with its own constitutional set-up, Azad Jammu and Kashmir does not send representatives to the National Assembly or Senate.

questions.text: The Capital Development Authority (CDA), responsible for planning and developing Islamabad, was established in
questions.explanation: The CDA was set up in 1960 under the Ayub Khan government to plan and build the new federal capital.

questions.text: Pakistan's State Emblem, like the national anthem, was formally adopted in
questions.explanation: The State Emblem was adopted in 1954, the same year as the national anthem.

questions.text: On the shield of Pakistan's State Emblem, cotton, wheat and jute appear alongside a fourth crop, which is
questions.explanation: The four quarters of the shield depict Pakistan's major crops: cotton, wheat, jute and tea.

questions.text: The scroll beneath the shield of Pakistan's State Emblem bears the national motto, which reads
questions.explanation: The State Emblem carries the motto "Unity, Faith, Discipline", attributed to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

questions.text: The design of Pakistan's national flag was based on the flag previously used by
questions.explanation: The green flag with a crescent and star, adopted as the national flag with an added white stripe, was based on the flag of the All-India Muslim League.

questions.text: The width-to-length ratio of Pakistan's national flag is
questions.explanation: The official specification for Pakistan's flag sets its width-to-length ratio at 2:3.

questions.text: On the national flag of Pakistan, the crescent is generally taken to symbolise progress, while the five-pointed star symbolises
questions.explanation: In the standard official description, the crescent stands for progress and the star for light and knowledge.

questions.text: Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore was built to commemorate
options: The founding of the Muslim League in 1906
questions.explanation: The tower marks the site where the Pakistan (Lahore) Resolution was passed by the All-India Muslim League in March 1940.

questions.text: The park in Lahore where Minar-e-Pakistan stands was originally known, in the colonial era, as
questions.explanation: The site, now called Iqbal Park, was known as Minto Park before independence.

questions.text: Mazar-e-Quaid, the mausoleum of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, is located in
questions.explanation: Mazar-e-Quaid, completed in 1970, stands in Karachi, where Jinnah is buried.

questions.text: The Pakistan Monument, a structure shaped like a blooming flower symbolising national unity, stands on the Shakarparian Hills in
questions.explanation: The Pakistan Monument was built on the Shakarparian Hills in Islamabad and inaugurated in 2007.

questions.text: The four large petals of the Pakistan Monument represent
options: The four founders of the Muslim League
The four rivers of the Indus system
The four pillars of the state
questions.explanation: The monument's four large petals symbolise Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

questions.text: Islamabad Capital Territory, distinct from all four provinces, is administered directly by the
questions.explanation: As a federal territory, Islamabad is administered directly by the Federal Government rather than by a provincial government.
